description: This report from Berkeley Lab and Rockcress Consulting, dated January 2025, creates three conceptual virtual power plant (VPP) profiles and a VPP inventory for the United States. It follows interviews with 24 subject matter experts on the challenges of scaling VPPs, which found a lack of clear, consistent language for describing VPP types and a shortage of information on current VPP trends. The profiles are Aggregated, Integrated and Orchestrated VPPs, each with a profile summary table. The inventory has a structure section and an inventory analysis that leverages a research dataset and the EIA distributed energy resource dataset, with analyses by VPP program implementor type, VPP type, potential VPP capacity, DER types and equity attributes, existing demand response programmes and net energy metering resources by state, and the potential to scale VPPs. Coverage is the United States. Access: PDF, free; the inventory is presented in the report and no separate data file was seen. Caveats: a point-in-time inventory built from research and EIA data. It suits distributed flexibility and capacity planning studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
